parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module's three files are all infrastructure code, but they don't present one consistent abstraction or boundary. InMemoryTaskRepository is an adapter behind a domain port (it implements ITaskRepository). InfraLogger is a concrete adapter with no port, and the application consumes the class directly (CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS edge to InfraLogger). InfraFormatters.formatDate is a generic, domain-agnostic utility rather than an adapter. The application re-exports it through TaskUtils, so it works as a shared helper, not part of the infrastructure boundary. Date formatting is also scattered: InfraLogger formats timestamps inline with new Date().toISOString() in both log() and error(), while InfraFormatters holds a separate toISOString-based formatting rule. The mix of port-backed adapters, concrete port-less adapters and general utilities means the module doesn't use one consistent abstraction. Import direction is out of scope and was not used as the basis for this judgment.
